aim: Causal evidence of whether event memory can adapt to changed reward mappings and recover previously useful preferences after an A-B-A return

online_adaptation.stage_B_reward_targets: two label preferences selected via seed-specific derangement of initial A context targets
online_adaptation.stage_A_return: exact initial A hidden preferences; no phase signal to learner

constants.archive_recall_trigger: 3 failures in last 4 outcome updates with archived expected success greater than recent by >=0.15

metrics: false switches on original A stage
checkpoint restoration replay and forged-state rejection
limits: Context and decoded event labels engineered; no hidden phase or target provided to memory
All methods receive same number of episodes and their own binary feedback only
No test feedback updates weights; previously inspected seeds are not blind
Any hyperparameter or protocol adjustment after observed test scores must be explicitly reported exploratory
Report learned-vs-simple baseline failures and task shift regressions
No unreviewed promotion, OS commands, AthenZ identity data or Synveil permissions
Retain V2A and V2B order and D1 D3 D4 gate status
